definitions.explanation: Expressing one's thoughts or feelings honestly and directly without concealment or pretense. Carries a positive nuance of sincerity rather than rudeness.

examples.japanese: {率直|そっちょく}な{意見|いけん}を{聞|き}きたい。
examples.english: I want to hear your frank opinion.

examples.japanese: {率直|そっちょく}に{言|い}って、この{計画|けいかく}には{問題|もんだい}がある。
examples.english: Frankly speaking, there are problems with this plan.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}は{率直|そっちょく}な{性格|せいかく}で、{思|おも}ったことをそのまま{口|くち}にする。
examples.english: He has a candid personality and says exactly what he thinks.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a na-adjective ({率直|そっちょく}な) or adverbially ({率直|そっちょく}に). The phrase {率直|そっちょく}に{言|い}って ("frankly speaking") is a common set expression used to preface an honest statement. Unlike {正直|しょうじき} which emphasizes moral honesty, {率直|そっちょく} focuses on directness of expression.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {率直|そっちょく}な{意見|いけん}: frank opinion
- {率直|そっちょく}な{感想|かんそう}: candid impression
- {率直|そっちょく}に{言|い}う: to speak frankly
- {率直|そっちょく}な{性格|せいかく}: straightforward personality
- {率直|そっちょく}に{認|みと}める: to admit candidly
